raw_response:
I farm only 3.5 mu, so I cannot take big risks. What I do is mostly what has kept the land giving grain over the years. Wheat and maize together are my safety. If one side is not so good, maybe the other side can still carry the year. I do not have much cash to throw around, and with people doing off-farm work, labor has to be simple and timed right.

For wheat, I will still sow around early October, same as our place usually does. I do not dare sow too late because then the seedlings are weak going into winter. I use the common seed from the local dealer, not the expensive fancy kind. Fertilizer, I will put a fair base dressing before sowing, then one topdressing when the wheat starts to stand up and grow fast in spring. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than see the wheat turn yellow and lose yield. Water costs money from the well, but wheat here usually needs a few turns, so I will irrigate about three times if rain is not enough.

For maize, I plant as soon as the wheat comes off, no waiting. In our place that gap is tight, so I keep the field work simple, just quick residue clearing and shallow tillage or direct planting if I can arrange it. Maize also gets some base fertilizer and one more feeding later. If summer rain is normal, maybe I only irrigate once or even not at all, but if it stays dry after sowing I will use the well because missing emergence is worse than paying some pumping money. I only spray when I really see weeds or insects. On such a small piece, every yuan matters, so I do enough to keep the crop safe, not more.
